chunks: From him, from Safwan and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-muzara'ah (sharecropping), and he said: 'The expenses are from you, and the land belongs to its owner; whatever Allah brings forth of anything is divided according to the condition. And thus the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) accepted Khaybar; they came to him and he gave it to them on the condition that they cultivate it, with the stipulation that they have half of what it produces. When the dates ripened, he ordered Abdullah ibn Rawahah to estimate the value of the palm trees for them. When he finished, he gave them the choice and said: "We have estimated this palm grove at so many sa'ns. If you wish, take it and return half of that to us; and if you wish, we will take it and give you half of that." The Jews said: "By this, the heavens and the earth stand."'

key_terms.النَّفَقَة: Expenses; costs incurred for cultivation such as seeds, tools, or labor.
key_terms.الْمُزَارَعَة: Sharecropping; an agricultural contract where one party provides land and the other labor, sharing the produce.
key_terms.خَرَصَ: To estimate or appraise the value of a crop or property in kind.
key_terms.خَيْبَر: Khaybar; a fertile oasis region in Arabia known for its date palms, given to Muslims as war booty.
key_terms.صَاعاً: Sa'; a traditional unit of volume used for measuring dry goods like dates or grain.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on sharecropping (muzara'ah) and how did the Prophet Muhammad apply it in Khaybar?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanics of *muzara'ah* by distinguishing between capital expenses borne by the cultivator and land ownership retained by the proprietor, with produce divided per agreement. It anchors this ruling in the historical precedent of Khaybar, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) accepted the land from the Jews on the condition that they cultivate it for half the yield, a practice validated by their own recognition of its justice. This establishes a foundational model for agricultural partnerships in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing mutual consent and equitable distribution of labor and land value.
